- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥2% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in that window.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for lagged mean reversion.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns bullish after day 15, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for days 20–30.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
